requirements.statement: Open with a Summary section: one paragraph on who, what, where, and the decision.
Then a Facts section. Every fact cites the document in the file it comes from, in square brackets: [notice of loss], [police report], [invoice 1].

source: (text, request, material) => { const names = material.map(m => m.name.toLowerCase()); const m = text.match(/## Facts\s*\n([\s\S]*?)(?=\n## |$)/i); if (!m) return null; const body = m[1]; const sentences = body.split(/(?<=[.!?])\s+/).map(s => s.trim()).filter(s => /[A-Za-z0-9]/.test(s)); const spans = []; for (const s of sentences) { const cites = [...s.matchAll(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g)].map(x => x[1].trim().toLowerCase()); const ok = cites.length > 0 && cites.every(c => names.includes(c)); if (!ok) { const idx = text.indexOf(s); spans.push({ start: Math.max(0, idx), end: Math.max(0, idx) + s.length, why: 'fact sentence without a bracketed citation to a document in the file' }); } } return { ok: spans.length === 0, detail: spans.length ? spans.length + ' uncited fact sentence(s)' : 'every fact cites a file document', spans }; }
means: Each sentence in the Facts section carries a bracketed citation, and each cited name is a document in the material.

requirements.statement: Then a Coverage analysis section. The coverage conclusion cites the policy clause it rests on, and every exclusion that could apply is addressed and cited.

source: (text, request, material) => { const m = text.match(/^##\s*Coverage analysis[\s\S]*?(?=^##\s|$(?![\s\S]))/im); if (!m) return null; const body = m[0]; const names = material.map(x => x.name.toLowerCase()); const spans = []; if (!/clause\s+\d+(\.\d+)*|\bsection\s+\d+(\.\d+)*/i.test(body)) spans.push({ start: 0, end: body.length, why: 'coverage conclusion cites no policy clause' }); const excl = [...body.matchAll(/exclusion\s+\d+(\.\d+)*/gi)]; for (const e of excl) { const after = body.slice(e.index, e.index + 250); if (!/\[[^\]]+\]/.test(after)) spans.push({ start: e.index, end: e.index + e[0].length, why: 'exclusion cited without a bracketed document' }); } const bad = []; for (const c of body.matchAll(/\[([^\]]+)\]/g)) { if (!names.includes(c[1].trim().toLowerCase())) bad.push({ start: c.index, end: c.index + c[0].length, why: 'citation not a document in the file' }); } return { ok: spans.length === 0 && bad.length === 0, detail: spans.length + bad.length ? 'coverage conclusion or exclusion citation missing' : 'coverage cites a clause and each exclusion cites a document', spans: spans.concat(bad) }; }
means: The Coverage analysis section cites a policy clause for its conclusion, and each exclusion it names is followed by a bracketed document citation. Whether every applicable exclusion was addressed is le

requirements.statement: Then a Decision section: covered or not covered, and under which clause.

source: if (!m) return { ok: false, detail: 'no Decision section', spans: [] };
return { ok, detail: ok ? 'decision states coverage and a clause' : 'decision lacks coverage status or clause number', spans: [] };
means: The Decision section states covered or not covered and names a clause number.

requirements.statement: Never speculate about the insured's intent or honesty.

source: (text, request, material) => { const re = /\b(intend|intent|intention|honest|dishonest|motive|motivated|deliberate|deliberately|wanted to|meant to|lying|lied|trying to deceive)\w*/gi; const spans = []; let m; while ((m = re.exec(text))) { spans.push({ start: m.index, end: m.index + m[0].length, why: 'speculation about intent or honesty' }); } return { ok: spans.length === 0, detail: spans.length ? spans.length + ' speculative term(s)' : 'no speculation about intent or honesty', spans }; }
means: No words about the insured's intent or honesty appear in the text.

requirements.statement: Every figure in the work is one the request or the material gives.
I keep paragraphs to 5 sentences at most.
I hedge rarely: at most 2 hedging words per thousand.
The Summary section runs 25 to 33 words in my pieces.
The Facts section runs 47 to 65 words in my pieces.

Write none of the moves that mark text as machine-written (announcing an insight others "miss", grading your own list, "the single most", announcing candour, "that's the whole game", reading the reader's mind, one thing "wearing another's clothes", a contrastive verdict as the opening line, an em dash, a run of three or more very short sentences).
No mechanical errors: spelling, agreement, punctuation.
